title: Risk Level for Children Aged 12 and Under Given Shift Back to Phase Two
what_it_is: Risk Level for Children Aged 12 and Under Given Shift Back to Phase Two

sections.label: COVID-19 in children under 12
sections.summary: International data and Singapore cases show milder COVID-19 disease in children under 12, with none needing ICU care or oxygen.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For children, international experience and data on COVID-19 infections have thus far shown that the disease outcome is much less severe as compared to older adults and the elderly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have so far observed mild disease in local cases aged under 12 years, even with the Delta variant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We are also fortunate thus far that for our children under 12 years who have been infected, none of them has required ICU care nor oxygen supplementation.

sections.label: Expert Committee monitoring vaccination trials
sections.summary: The Expert Committee on COVID-19 Vaccination is monitoring vaccination trials for children under 12 and will recommend to MOH when suitable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Expert Committee on COVID-19 Vaccination or EC19V as we call it, is monitoring on-going vaccination trials for children under the age of 12.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The EC19V will assess if it is suitable to administer these vaccines to children under the age of 12 and make recommendations to MOH at the appropriate time.

sections.label: No timeline for child vaccines
sections.summary: The timeline depends on work by the committee and vaccine manufacturers, and a vaccine for under-12s is unlikely anytime soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That very much will depend on the work that they are doing and also from the work that the manufacturers of the vaccines are doing now, worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, at this point in time, I am unable to give a timeline as to when this work will be completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Like Ms He Ting Ru, I think all of us, as parents, are, of course, concerned with the safety of our children under the age of 12 who are unable to be vaccinated yet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And we also know that we are unlikely to have a vaccine for those under 12 years old, anytime soon.

sections.label: Safe management measures and adult vaccination
sections.summary: Safe management measures like personal hygiene and class cohorting are practised, and adults are encouraged to get vaccinated soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: One, we want to make sure that we observe all the safe management measures that we can practise: personal hygiene, cohorting of the classes to minimise the chances of our younger children getting it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And I think, to this extent, the adults also have a role to play, which is why we encourage everyone to try to get vaccinated as soon as possible.

sections.label: Less intrusive mass testing capabilities
sections.summary: Future less intrusive mass testing capabilities could allow more activities by testing more people regularly, including younger ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Going forward, if and when the day comes whereby we have other testing capabilities that are less intrusive, that we can conduct on a mass scale, that will give us yet another tool for us to see how we can safely have more activities by testing more people more regularly, including perhaps the younger ones.
